newsitem.title: UK: Studies show link between HRT and thrombosis.
newsitem.headline: Studies show link between HRT and thrombosis.

text.p: Women taking hormone replacement therapy after going through the menopause could face an increased risk of blots clots, doctors said on Friday.
In three separate studies published in the Lancet medical journal doctors reported HRT users were more likely to develop blood clots in the leg and lungs.
Blood clots have been associated with the use of the oral contraceptive pill but research has not confirmed a link with HRT.

"Each of the three studies shows a twofold to fourfold risk of venous thromboembolism (blood clots) with oestrogen-only as well as with combined oestrogen-progestagen hormone-replacement therapy," Jan P Vandenbroucke and Frans Helmerhorst of the University of Leiden in the Netherlands said in a commentary.
HRT is a drug therapy to relieve the symptoms of the menopause which can include hot flushes, irritability, depression, palpitations and headaches.
It is also reported to help protect women against heart disease and osteoporosis or brittle bone disease. But it has been linked to a slight increase in breast cancer.
Hershel Jick and colleagues at Boston University Medical Centre in Lexington, Massachusetts studied women aged 50-74 who had been admitted to the hospital with blood clots from 1980-1994.
They found the risk of thromboembolism was "three times higher among current users of replacement oestrogen than among non-users."

Vandenbroucke recommended that doctors and patients should take account of the risk factors for blood clotting, including a family history, gross obsesity and a previous episode, and weigh them against the benefits of HRT.
